entries.title: II Timothy 4:6
segments: The time of my departure. Tradition records the death of Paul by execution in the early summer of the year 68 A.D.  This second epistle to Timothy was written but a few weeks previous.  It is probable that Paul had  a clear premonition of his approaching end.

entries.title: II Timothy 4:10
segments: Forsook me. It would seem that as the execution of Paul became certain, their was a scattering of some of his associates at Rome, lest they might suffer a like fate.  Demas and Luke had been with Paul when he wrote the letter to the Colossians about six years previous.  This was during Paul's first imprisonment.  See

.
 

 
 Loved this present world. Did not desire to suffer martyrdom.
 

 
 Dalmatia. A district of Roman Illyricum lying north of Macedonia.  It was a wild and barbarous country.

entries.title: II Timothy 4:16
segments: No one took my part. It was a custom in both the Roman and Greek courts to allow the friends of the accused to intercede with pleas and prayers for mercy.

entries.title: II Timothy 4:17
segments: The mouth of the lion. This expression may refer to the practice of throwing Christians to the wild beasts in the arena, a common penalty under Nero's rule.
